figures.observation: Upper barrier with A; spreading curved wavefronts reach a second barrier with B and C; two spreading wavefront families overlap below it and reach a lower screen. No numerical lengths or angle scale.
figures.use: Explain shared illumination, coherent secondary waves, spreading and overlap; curved strokes denote wavefronts rather than ray paths.
figures.uncertainty: Source stroke density and scan texture are not a reliable count of wave cycles or fringes.

figures.observation: Point source S on left, radius segment R to curved spherical wavefront, near-axis patch endpoints a and b, and horizontal line from S to observation point B on right.
figures.use: Identify the arc as a wavefront, not an opaque disk; distinguish a model surface patch and an effective straight propagation direction.
figures.uncertainty: Patch size is schematic and has no supplied number; do not infer exact cancellation everywhere outside it.

figures.observation: Three panels left to right: fine metal wire with longitudinal bands; circular hole with alternating concentric brightness and a dark-looking center; opaque circular object with central bright dot in dark shadow and surrounding ring-like pattern.
figures.use: Retain wire/opening/disk identities and qualitative brightness distribution, with Latin panel labels in both candidate texts.
figures.uncertainty: No scale or reliable exact ring count. The shown dark hole center is conditional, not universal.

figures.observation: Unlabeled monochrome historical portrait crop of a man in formal clothing, associated by source biography with Augustin Fresnel.
figures.use: Retain the source portrait subject identity only; biography stays bound to source text and dates.
figures.uncertainty: Pixels alone do not independently prove identity, image provenance, or archival authenticity. No generated or reused modern portrait is approved.
